originalComment: Compute the mean value of an diagonal observable.
codeComment: This function calculates the average of the values in the `counts` dictionary based on the weights provided in the `observable` dictionary. If `observable` is not a dictionary, it is converted to one using the `make_dict_observable` function. The function iterates over the keys in `counts`, multiplies the count by the corresponding weight from `observable`, and sums these products to compute the average.
codeFunctions: def average_data (counts,observable):if not isinstance (observable,dict):observable = make_dict_observable (observable) temp = 0 tot = sum (counts.values ()) for key in counts:if key in observable:temp += counts [ key ] * observable [ key ] / tot return temp

originalComment: Process an Id or IndexedId node as a bit or register type.
codeComment: This function processes a bit ID (either a qubit or a classical bit) and returns a list of tuples representing the bit or register. It first checks if the bit ID is a qubit or classical bit by looking it up in the DAG's qregs or cregs. If the bit ID is not found, it raises a QiskitError. If the bit ID is found, it checks if the bit ID is indexed or not. If it is indexed, it returns a list of tuples representing the indexed bit or qubit. If it is not indexed, it checks if the bit ID is a local bit or a global bit. If it is a local bit, it returns the local bit. If it is a global bit, it returns a list of tuples representing all the bits in the register. If the bit ID is not found in the local or global scope, it raises a QiskitError.
codeFunctions: def _process_bit_id (self,node):# pylint: disable=inconsistent-return-statements reg = None if node.name in self.dag.qregs:reg = self.dag.qregs [ node.name ] elif node.name in self.dag.cregs:reg = self.dag.cregs [ node.name ] else:raise QiskitError ("expected qreg or creg name:","line=%s" % node.line,"file=%s" % node.file) if node.type == "indexed_id":# An indexed bit or qubit return [ (reg,node.index) ] elif node.type == "id":# A qubit or qreg or creg if not self.bit_stack [ - 1 ]:# Global scope return [ (reg,j) for j in range (reg.size) ] else:# local scope if node.name in self.bit_stack [ - 1 ]:return [ self.bit_stack [ - 1 ] [ node.name ] ] raise QiskitError ("expected local bit name:","line=%s" % node.line,"file=%s" % node.file) return None

originalComment: Process a custom unitary node.
codeComment: This function processes a custom unitary node in a quantum circuit. It checks if the node has arguments and processes them accordingly. It then processes the bitlist and extracts the relevant bits. If the gate name is defined in the gates dictionary, it creates a DAG operation using the processed arguments and bits. If the gate name is not defined, it raises a QiskitError.
codeFunctions: def _process_custom_unitary (self,node):name = node.name if node.arguments is not None:args = self._process_node (node.arguments) else:args = [ ] bits = [ self._process_bit_id (node_element) for node_element in node.bitlist.children ] if name in self.gates:gargs = self.gates [ name ] [ "args" ] gbits = self.gates [ name ] [ "bits" ] # Loop over register arguments, if any. maxidx = max (map (len,bits)) for idx in range (maxidx):self.arg_stack.append ({ gargs [ j ]:args [ j ] for j in range (len (gargs)) }) # Only index into register arguments. element = [ idx * x for x in [ len (bits [ j ]) > 1 for j in range (len (bits)) ] ] self.bit_stack.append ({ gbits [ j ]:bits [ j ] [ element [ j ] ] for j in range (len (gbits)) }) self._create_dag_op (name,[ self.arg_stack [ - 1 ] [ s ].sym () for s in gargs ],[ self.bit_stack [ - 1 ] [ s ] for s in gbits ]) self.arg_stack.pop () self.bit_stack.pop () else:raise QiskitError ("internal error undefined gate:","line=%s" % node.line,"file=%s" % node.file)

originalComment: Process a CNOT gate node.
codeComment: This function processes a CNOT gate node in a quantum circuit. It checks if the bit IDs of the two qubits involved in the CNOT gate are of the same length or if one of them is a single qubit. If the conditions are not met, it raises a QiskitError. It then applies the CNOT gate to the appropriate qubits based on the lengths of the bit IDs.

originalComment: Process a measurement node.

codeFunctions: def _create_dag_op (self,name,params,qargs):if name == "u0":op_class = U0Gate elif name == "u1":op_class = U1Gate elif name == "u2":op_class = U2Gate elif name == "u3":op_class = U3Gate elif name == "x":op_class = XGate elif name == "y":op_class = YGate elif name == "z":op_class = ZGate elif name == "t":op_class = TGate elif name == "tdg":op_class = TdgGate elif name == "s":op_class = SGate elif name == "sdg":op_class = SdgGate elif name == "swap":op_class = SwapGate elif name == "rx":op_class = RXGate elif name == "ry":op_class = RYGate elif name == "rz":op_class = RZGate elif name == "rzz":op_class = RZZGate elif name == "id":op_class = IdGate elif name == "h":op_class = HGate elif name == "cx":op_class = CnotGate elif name == "cy":op_class = CyGate elif name == "cz":op_class = CzGate elif name == "ch":op_class = CHGate elif name == "crz":op_class = CrzGate elif name == "cu1":op_class = Cu1Gate elif name == "cu3":op_class = Cu3Gate elif name == "ccx":op_class = ToffoliGate elif name == "cswap":op_class = FredkinGate else:raise QiskitError ("unknown operation for ast node name %s" % name) op = op_class (* params) self.dag.apply_operation_back (op,qargs,[ ],condition = self.condition)

codeFunctions: def check_type (self,value,attr,data):expected_types = self._expected_types () if not isinstance (value,expected_types):raise self._not_expected_type (value,expected_types,fields = [ self ],field_names = attr,data = data) return value

originalComment: Include unknown fields after dumping.
codeComment: This function takes three parameters: `valid_data`, `many`, and `original_data`. It checks if `many` is True. If it is, it iterates over `valid_data` and for each element, it finds the additional keys in `original_data` that are not present in `valid_data` and adds them to `valid_data`. If `many` is False, it does the same but for the entire `original_data`. The function returns the modified `valid_data`.
codeFunctions: def dump_additional_data (self,valid_data,many,original_data):if many:for i,_ in enumerate (valid_data):additional_keys = set (original_data [ i ].__dict__) - set (valid_data [ i ]) for key in additional_keys:valid_data [ i ] [ key ] = getattr (original_data [ i ],key) else:additional_keys = set (original_data.__dict__) - set (valid_data) for key in additional_keys:valid_data [ key ] = getattr (original_data,key) return valid_data

originalComment: Include unknown fields after load.
codeComment: This function takes three parameters: `valid_data`, `many`, and `original_data`. It checks if `many` is True. If it is, it iterates over `valid_data` and for each element, it finds the keys in `original_data` that are not present in the current element of `valid_data`. It then adds these keys and their corresponding values to the current element of `valid_data`. If `many` is False, it finds the keys in `original_data` that are not present in any element of `valid_data` and adds these keys and their corresponding values to `valid_data`. Finally, it returns the modified `valid_data`.
codeFunctions: def load_additional_data (self,valid_data,many,original_data):if many:for i,_ in enumerate (valid_data):additional_keys = set (original_data [ i ]) - set (valid_data [ i ]) for key in additional_keys:valid_data [ i ] [ key ] = original_data [ i ] [ key ] else:additional_keys = set (original_data) - set (valid_data) for key in additional_keys:valid_data [ key ] = original_data [ key ] return valid_data

originalComment: n - qubit QFT on q in circ.
codeComment: The function `qft` performs a Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) on a quantum circuit `circ` with `n` qubits. It iterates over each qubit `j` from 0 to `n-1`, and for each qubit `j`, it applies a series of CNOT and Hadamard gates to transform the state of the qubits. The CNOT gates are applied in a way that effectively rotates the state of the qubits, and the Hadamard gates are applied to the qubit `j` itself.
codeFunctions: def qft (circ,q,n):for j in range (n):for k in range (j):circ.cu1 (math.pi / float (2 ** (j - k)),q [ j ],q [ k ]) circ.h (q [ j ])

originalComment: Partial trace over subsystems of multi - partite vector.
codeComment: This function takes a vector `vec`, a list of systems to trace out, and the dimensions of the system. It reshapes the vector into a tensor, traces out the specified systems, and returns the resulting tensor.
codeFunctions: def __partial_trace_vec (vec,trace_systems,dimensions,reverse = True):# trace sys positions if reverse:dimensions = dimensions [::- 1 ] trace_systems = len (dimensions) - 1 - np.array (trace_systems) rho = vec.reshape (dimensions) rho = np.tensordot (rho,rho.conj (),axes = (trace_systems,trace_systems)) d = int (np.sqrt (np.product (rho.shape))) return rho.reshape (d,d)

originalComment: Flatten an operator to a vector in a specified basis.
codeComment: This function takes a density matrix and a method as input. If the method is 'col', it flattens the matrix in column-major order. If the method is 'row', it flattens the matrix in row-major order. If the method is 'pauli' or 'pauli_weights', it calculates the trace of the product of each Pauli matrix in the Pauli group of the same dimension as the density matrix and returns the result as a numpy array. If the input state is not an n-qubit state, it raises an exception.
codeFunctions: def vectorize (density_matrix,method = 'col'):density_matrix = np.array (density_matrix) if method == 'col':return density_matrix.flatten (order = 'F') elif method == 'row':return density_matrix.flatten (order = 'C') elif method in [ 'pauli','pauli_weights' ]:num = int (np.log2 (len (density_matrix))) # number of qubits if len (density_matrix) != 2 ** num:raise Exception ('Input state must be n-qubit state') if method == 'pauli_weights':pgroup = pauli_group (num,case = 'weight') else:pgroup = pauli_group (num,case = 'tensor') vals = [ np.trace (np.dot (p.to_matrix (),density_matrix)) for p in pgroup ] return np.array (vals) return None

originalComment: Devectorize a vectorized square matrix.
codeComment: This function takes a vectorized matrix and converts it back into a square matrix. It supports two methods: 'col' for column-major order and 'row' for row-major order. If the input is not a vectorized square matrix, it raises an exception. If the method is 'pauli' or 'pauli_weights', it converts the vectorized matrix into a matrix of Pauli operators or their weights, respectively.
codeFunctions: def devectorize (vectorized_mat,method = 'col'):vectorized_mat = np.array (vectorized_mat) dimension = int (np.sqrt (vectorized_mat.size)) if len (vectorized_mat) != dimension * dimension:raise Exception ('Input is not a vectorized square matrix') if method == 'col':return vectorized_mat.reshape (dimension,dimension,order = 'F') elif method == 'row':return vectorized_mat.reshape (dimension,dimension,order = 'C') elif method in [ 'pauli','pauli_weights' ]:num_qubits = int (np.log2 (dimension)) # number of qubits if dimension != 2 ** num_qubits:raise Exception ('Input state must be n-qubit state') if method == 'pauli_weights':pgroup = pauli_group (num_qubits,case = 'weight') else:pgroup = pauli_group (num_qubits,case = 'tensor') pbasis = np.array ([ p.to_matrix () for p in pgroup ]) / 2 ** num_qubits return np.tensordot (vectorized_mat,pbasis,axes = 1) return None

originalComment: Convert a Choi - matrix to a Pauli - basis superoperator.
codeComment: This function calculates the Choi-Ruali matrix for a given Choi matrix `choi` and an optional order parameter. The Choi-Ruali matrix is a representation of a quantum channel in terms of Pauli operators. The function first determines the number of qubits based on the length of the Choi matrix. It then creates a Pauli group with the specified order ('weight' or 'tensor') and iterates over all pairs of Pauli operators to compute the Choi-Ruali matrix. The result is reshaped into a square matrix of size \(4^n\), where \(n\) is the number of qubits.
codeFunctions: def choi_to_rauli (choi,order = 1):if order == 0:order = 'weight' elif order == 1:order = 'tensor' # get number of qubits' num_qubits = int (np.log2 (np.sqrt (len (choi)))) pgp = pauli_group (num_qubits,case = order) rauli = [ ] for i in pgp:for j in pgp:pauliop = np.kron (j.to_matrix ().T,i.to_matrix ()) rauli += [ np.trace (np.dot (choi,pauliop)) ] return np.array (rauli).reshape (4 ** num_qubits,4 ** num_qubits)

originalComment: Truncate small values of a complex array.
codeComment: This function takes an array and an optional epsilon parameter (default is 1e-10). It checks if the array is real or complex. If real, it sets elements with absolute value less than epsilon to 0. If complex, it sets the real and imaginary parts of elements with absolute value less than epsilon to 0. The function returns the modified array.
codeFunctions: def chop (array,epsilon = 1e-10):ret = np.array (array) if np.isrealobj (ret):ret [ abs (ret) < epsilon ] = 0.0 else:ret.real [ abs (ret.real) < epsilon ] = 0.0 ret.imag [ abs (ret.imag) < epsilon ] = 0.0 return ret

originalComment: Construct the outer product of two vectors.
codeComment: This function takes two vectors as input. If the second vector is not provided, it defaults to the conjugate of the first vector. It then returns the outer product of the two vectors.
codeFunctions: def outer (vector1,vector2 = None):if vector2 is None:vector2 = np.array (vector1).conj () else:vector2 = np.array (vector2).conj () return np.outer (vector1,vector2)

originalComment: Calculate the concurrence.
codeComment: The function `concurrence` calculates the concurrence of a quantum state. It first checks if the input state is a 1D array and converts it to a 2D array using the outer product. If the state has fewer than 4 qubits, it raises an exception. The function then defines a matrix `YY` and computes the concurrence using the formula involving the state, `YY`, and its conjugate transpose. The eigenvalues of the resulting matrix are calculated, and the concurrence is computed as the maximum of 0 and the difference between the largest eigenvalue and the sum of the other eigenvalues.
codeFunctions: def concurrence (state):rho = np.array (state) if rho.ndim == 1:rho = outer (state) if len (state) != 4:raise Exception ("Concurrence is only defined for more than two qubits") YY = np.fliplr (np.diag ([ - 1,1,1,- 1 ])) A = rho.dot (YY).dot (rho.conj ()).dot (YY) w = la.eigh (A,eigvals_only = True) w = np.sqrt (np.maximum (w,0)) return max (0.0,w [ - 1 ] - np.sum (w [ 0:- 1 ]))

originalComment: Compute the Shannon entropy of a probability vector.
codeComment: The function `shannon_entropy` calculates the Shannon entropy of a probability vector `pvec`. It takes an optional `base` parameter, which defaults to 2. The function uses a logarithmic function `logfn` to compute the entropy based on the specified base. The entropy is calculated as the sum of the logarithmic values of each probability in the vector, weighted by the probability itself.
codeFunctions: def shannon_entropy (pvec,base = 2):# pylint: disable=missing-docstring if base == 2:def logfn (x):return - x * np.log2 (x) elif base == np.e:def logfn (x):return - x * np.log (x) else:def logfn (x):return - x * np.log (x) / np.log (base) h = 0. for x in pvec:if 0 < x < 1:h += logfn (x) return h

originalComment: Compute the von - Neumann entropy of a quantum state.
codeComment: This function calculates the entropy of a given quantum state represented by a density matrix. It first checks if the input state is a 1D array, in which case it returns 0 as the entropy. Otherwise, it computes the eigenvalues of the state matrix, filters out the negative values, and then calculates the Shannon entropy of the resulting eigenvalues using the `shannon_entropy` function.
codeFunctions: def entropy (state):rho = np.array (state) if rho.ndim == 1:return 0 evals = np.maximum (np.linalg.eigvalsh (state),0.) return shannon_entropy (evals,base = np.e)

originalComment: Compute the mutual information of a bipartite state.
codeComment: This function calculates the mutual information between two subsystems in a quantum state. It first checks if the second subsystem dimension `d1` is provided, and if not, it calculates it as half the length of the state. Then, it computes the mutual information by summing the entropies of the partial traces of the state over the two subsystems and subtracting the entropy of the entire state.
codeFunctions: def mutual_information (state,d0,d1 = None):if d1 is None:d1 = int (len (state) / d0) mi = entropy (partial_trace (state,[ 0 ],dimensions = [ d0,d1 ])) mi += entropy (partial_trace (state,[ 1 ],dimensions = [ d0,d1 ])) mi -= entropy (state) return mi

originalComment: Compute the entanglement of formation of quantum state.
codeComment: This function calculates the entanglement of formation (EOF) of a given quantum state. It first checks if the input is a valid state-vector or 2-qubit density matrix. If the input is a state-vector, it calculates the EOF using the `__eof_qubit` function. If the input is a 2-qubit density matrix, it traces out the largest dimension and calculates the EOF using the `entropy` function. If the input is neither a state-vector nor a 2-qubit density matrix, it prints an error message and returns `None`.
codeFunctions: def entanglement_of_formation (state,d0,d1 = None):state = np.array (state) if d1 is None:d1 = int (len (state) / d0) if state.ndim == 2 and len (state) == 4 and d0 == 2 and d1 == 2:return __eof_qubit (state) elif state.ndim == 1:# trace out largest dimension if d0 < d1:tr = [ 1 ] else:tr = [ 0 ] state = partial_trace (state,tr,dimensions = [ d0,d1 ]) return entropy (state) else:print ('Input must be a state-vector or 2-qubit density matrix.') return None

originalComment: Compute the Entanglement of Formation of a 2 - qubit density matrix.
codeComment: This function calculates the Shannon entropy of a quantum state represented by a density matrix `rho`. It first computes the concurrence of the state using the `concurrence` function, then calculates the entanglement parameter `c` as `0.5 + 0.5 * sqrt(1 - c^2)`, and finally returns the Shannon entropy of the state `[c, 1 - c]`.
codeFunctions: def __eof_qubit (rho):c = concurrence (rho) c = 0.5 + 0.5 * np.sqrt (1 - c * c) return shannon_entropy ([ c,1 - c ])

codeComment: This function takes two `ScheduleComponent` objects, `parent` and `child`, and an optional `name` string. It finds the common channels between the two components, calculates the insertion time as the stop time of the parent component at the common channels, and then inserts the child component at that time with the given name. codeFunctions: def append (parent:ScheduleComponent,child:ScheduleComponent,name:str = None) -> Schedule:common_channels = set (parent.channels) & set (child.channels) insertion_time = parent.ch_stop_time (* common_channels) return insert (parent,insertion_time,child,name = name)

originalComment: Calculate the Hamming distance between two bit strings
codeComment: The function `hamming_distance` calculates the Hamming distance between two strings. It first checks if the lengths of the two strings are equal. If not, it raises a `VisualizationError` with the message "Strings not same length." If the lengths are equal, it calculates the Hamming distance by summing up the positions where the corresponding characters in the strings are different.

originalComment: Return quaternion for rotation about given axis.
codeComment: This function converts an axis-angle representation into a quaternion. It takes an angle and an axis (x, y, or z) as input and returns a quaternion object. The function first checks if the axis is valid, then calculates the quaternion components based on the angle and axis, and finally returns the quaternion.
codeFunctions: def quaternion_from_axis_rotation (angle,axis):out = np.zeros (4,dtype = float) if axis == 'x':out [ 1 ] = 1 elif axis == 'y':out [ 2 ] = 1 elif axis == 'z':out [ 3 ] = 1 else:raise ValueError ('Invalid axis input.') out *= math.sin (angle / 2.0) out [ 0 ] = math.cos (angle / 2.0) return Quaternion (out)

originalComment: Generate a quaternion from a set of Euler angles.
codeComment: This function converts Euler angles to a quaternion using the specified order. It first converts each Euler angle to a quaternion using the `quaternion_from_axis_rotation` function, then multiplies these quaternions together in the specified order, and finally normalizes the resulting quaternion.
codeFunctions: def quaternion_from_euler (angles,order = 'yzy'):angles = np.asarray (angles,dtype = float) quat = quaternion_from_axis_rotation (angles [ 0 ],order [ 0 ]) * (quaternion_from_axis_rotation (angles [ 1 ],order [ 1 ]) * quaternion_from_axis_rotation (angles [ 2 ],order [ 2 ])) quat.normalize (inplace = True) return quat

originalComment: Normalizes a Quaternion to unit length so that it represents a valid rotation.
codeComment: This function normalizes the quaternion data. If `inplace` is `True`, it normalizes the data in place and returns `None`. If `inplace` is `False`, it creates a copy of the data, normalizes it, and returns a new Quaternion object with the normalized data.
codeFunctions: def normalize (self,inplace = False):if inplace:nrm = self.norm () self.data /= nrm return None nrm = self.norm () data_copy = np.array (self.data,copy = True) data_copy /= nrm return Quaternion (data_copy)

originalComment: Converts a unit - length quaternion to a rotation matrix.
codeComment: This function converts a normalized quaternion to a rotation matrix. It first normalizes the quaternion using the `normalize()` method and then constructs a rotation matrix using the quaternion components. The matrix is returned as a NumPy array with float data type.
codeFunctions: def to_matrix (self):w,x,y,z = self.normalize ().data # pylint: disable=C0103 mat = np.array ([ [ 1 - 2 * y ** 2 - 2 * z ** 2,2 * x * y - 2 * z * w,2 * x * z + 2 * y * w ],[ 2 * x * y + 2 * z * w,1 - 2 * x ** 2 - 2 * z ** 2,2 * y * z - 2 * x * w ],[ 2 * x * z - 2 * y * w,2 * y * z + 2 * x * w,1 - 2 * x ** 2 - 2 * y ** 2 ] ],dtype = float) return mat

originalComment: Converts a unit - length quaternion to a sequence of ZYZ Euler angles.
codeComment: This function converts a matrix to Euler angles using the ZYX convention. It first checks the value of the third element in the third row of the matrix. If it is between -1 and 1, it calculates the Euler angles using the atan2 and acos functions. If the value is outside this range, it calculates the Euler angles using the atan2 function with negative values. The function returns the Euler angles as a numpy array.
codeFunctions: def to_zyz (self):mat = self.to_matrix () euler = np.zeros (3,dtype = float) if mat [ 2,2 ] < 1:if mat [ 2,2 ] > - 1:euler [ 0 ] = math.atan2 (mat [ 1,2 ],mat [ 0,2 ]) euler [ 1 ] = math.acos (mat [ 2,2 ]) euler [ 2 ] = math.atan2 (mat [ 2,1 ],- mat [ 2,0 ]) else:euler [ 0 ] = - math.atan2 (mat [ 1,0 ],mat [ 1,1 ]) euler [ 1 ] = np.pi else:euler [ 0 ] = math.atan2 (mat [ 1,0 ],mat [ 1,1 ]) return euler

originalComment: Prepare received data for representation.

codeFunctions: def process_data (data,number_to_keep):result = dict () if number_to_keep != 0:data_temp = dict (Counter (data).most_common (number_to_keep)) data_temp [ 'rest' ] = sum (data.values ()) - sum (data_temp.values ()) data = data_temp labels = data values = np.array ([ data [ key ] for key in labels ],dtype = float) pvalues = values / sum (values) for position,label in enumerate (labels):result [ label ] = round (pvalues [ position ],5) return result

It first calls the `check_type` method of the superclass `InstructionParameter` to ensure the value is of the correct type. If the value is a collection, it recursively checks each item in the collection. The function returns the result of the superclass check.

originalComment: Check that j is a valid index into self.
codeComment: This function checks if the input `j` is an integer or a slice and raises a `QiskitIndexError` if it is out of range. If `j` is an integer, it checks if it is less than 0 or greater than or equal to the size of the register. If `j` is a slice, it checks if the start is less than 0, the stop is greater than or equal to the size, and the step is not None and less than or equal to 0.
codeFunctions: def check_range (self,j):if isinstance (j,int):if j < 0 or j >= self.size:raise QiskitIndexError ("register index out of range") elif isinstance (j,slice):if j.start < 0 or j.stop >= self.size or (j.step is not None and j.step <= 0):raise QiskitIndexError ("register index slice out of range")

originalComment: Test if an array is a diagonal matrix
codeComment: This function checks if a given matrix is a diagonal matrix. It first converts the input to a NumPy array and checks if it is a 2D matrix. If not, it returns False. Then, it checks if the matrix is equal to its diagonal using the `np.allclose` function with the specified relative and absolute tolerances.
codeFunctions: def is_diagonal_matrix (mat,rtol = RTOL_DEFAULT,atol = ATOL_DEFAULT):if atol is None:atol = ATOL_DEFAULT if rtol is None:rtol = RTOL_DEFAULT mat = np.array (mat) if mat.ndim != 2:return False return np.allclose (mat,np.diag (np.diagonal (mat)),rtol = rtol,atol = atol)

codeComment: This function checks if a given matrix is positive semidefinite. It first checks if the matrix is Hermitian, then calculates the eigenvalues of the matrix using `np.linalg.eigvalsh`. codeFunctions: def is_positive_semidefinite_matrix (mat,rtol = RTOL_DEFAULT,atol = ATOL_DEFAULT):if atol is None:atol = ATOL_DEFAULT if rtol is None:rtol = RTOL_DEFAULT if not is_hermitian_matrix (mat,rtol = rtol,atol = atol):return False # Check eigenvalues are all positive vals = np.linalg.eigvalsh (mat) for v in vals:if v < - atol:return False return True

originalComment: Test if an array is an identity matrix.
codeComment: This function checks if a given matrix is an identity matrix, considering optional parameters for tolerance and ignoring phase differences. The function returns `True` if the matrix is an identity matrix within the given tolerance, otherwise `False`.
codeFunctions: def is_identity_matrix (mat,ignore_phase = False,rtol = RTOL_DEFAULT,atol = ATOL_DEFAULT):if atol is None:atol = ATOL_DEFAULT if rtol is None:rtol = RTOL_DEFAULT mat = np.array (mat) if mat.ndim != 2:return False if ignore_phase:# If the matrix is equal to an identity up to a phase, we can # remove the phase by multiplying each entry by the complex # conjugate of the phase of the [0, 0] entry. theta = np.angle (mat [ 0,0 ]) mat = np.exp (- 1j * theta) * mat # Check if square identity iden = np.eye (len (mat)) return np.allclose (mat,iden,rtol = rtol,atol = atol)

originalComment: Test if an array is a unitary matrix.
codeComment: This function checks if a given matrix is unitary. It first converts the input matrix to a NumPy array. codeFunctions: def is_unitary_matrix (mat,rtol = RTOL_DEFAULT,atol = ATOL_DEFAULT):if atol is None:atol = ATOL_DEFAULT if rtol is None:rtol = RTOL_DEFAULT mat = np.array (mat) # Compute A^dagger.A and see if it is identity matrix mat = np.conj (mat.T).dot (mat) return is_identity_matrix (mat,ignore_phase = False,rtol = rtol,atol = atol)

originalComment: Transform Kraus representation to Choi representation.
codeComment: This function converts a set of Kraus operators into a Choi matrix. If there is only one Kraus operator, it computes the outer product of the operator with its conjugate. If there are two Kraus operators, it computes the outer product of each operator with the conjugate of the corresponding operator in the second set. The result is the Choi matrix, which is a matrix representation of the quantum channel.
codeFunctions: def _kraus_to_choi (data,input_dim,output_dim):choi = 0 kraus_l,kraus_r = data if kraus_r is None:for i in kraus_l:vec = i.ravel (order = 'F') choi += np.outer (vec,vec.conj ()) else:for i,j in zip (kraus_l,kraus_r):choi += np.outer (i.ravel (order = 'F'),j.ravel (order = 'F').conj ()) return choi

originalComment: Transform Choi representation to Kraus representation.
codeComment: This function converts a Choi matrix into a Kraus representation. It first checks if the Choi matrix is hermitian and then performs eigen-decomposition to get the Kraus representation. If the Choi matrix is not hermitian, it performs singular value decomposition (SVD) to get the Kraus representation. The function returns the Kraus representation as a list of matrices. If the Choi matrix is zero, it returns a single zero-element Kraus matrix.
codeFunctions: def _choi_to_kraus (data,input_dim,output_dim,atol = ATOL_DEFAULT):# Check if hermitian matrix if is_hermitian_matrix (data,atol = atol):# Get eigen-decomposition of Choi-matrix w,v = la.eigh (data) # Check eigenvaleus are non-negative if len (w [ w < - atol ]) == 0:# CP-map Kraus representation kraus = [ ] for val,vec in zip (w,v.T):if abs (val) > atol:k = np.sqrt (val) * vec.reshape ((output_dim,input_dim),order = 'F') kraus.append (k) # If we are converting a zero matrix, we need to return a Kraus set # with a single zero-element Kraus matrix if not kraus:kraus.append (np.zeros ((output_dim,input_dim),dtype = complex)) return (kraus,None) # Non-CP-map generalized Kraus representation mat_u,svals,mat_vh = la.svd (data) kraus_l = [ ] kraus_r = [ ] for val,vec_l,vec_r in zip (svals,mat_u.T,mat_vh.conj ()):kraus_l.append (np.sqrt (val) * vec_l.reshape ((output_dim,input_dim),order = 'F')) kraus_r.append (np.sqrt (val) * vec_r.reshape ((output_dim,input_dim),order = 'F')) return (kraus_l,kraus_r)

originalComment: Transform Stinespring representation to Kraus representation.
codeComment: This function takes a list of matrices `data` and converts each matrix into a list of Kraus operators. If a matrix is `None`, it appends `None` to the `kraus_pair`. Otherwise, it calculates the trace dimension, creates an identity matrix, and constructs the Kraus operators by taking the Kronecker product of the identity matrix with a vector of ones and then multiplying it with the input matrix. The resulting Kraus operators are appended to the `kraus_pair`. Finally, the function returns the `kraus_pair` as a tuple.
codeFunctions: def _stinespring_to_kraus (data,input_dim,output_dim):kraus_pair = [ ] for stine in data:if stine is None:kraus_pair.append (None) else:trace_dim = stine.shape [ 0 ] // output_dim iden = np.eye (output_dim) kraus = [ ] for j in range (trace_dim):vec = np.zeros (trace_dim) vec [ j ] = 1 kraus.append (np.kron (iden,vec [ None,:]).dot (stine)) kraus_pair.append (kraus) return tuple (kraus_pair)

originalComment: Transform Stinespring representation to Choi representation.
codeComment: This function takes two input arrays, `data[0]` and `data[1]`, and converts them into Choi matrices. It first calculates the trace dimension based on the input dimensions. Then, it reshapes the input arrays into matrices `stine_l` and `stine_r`. If `data[1]` is not provided, it sets `stine_r` to be the same as `stine_l`. Finally, it computes the Choi matrix using the Einstein summation convention and reshapes the result to have dimensions `[2 * input_dim * output_dim]`.
codeFunctions: def _stinespring_to_choi (data,input_dim,output_dim):trace_dim = data [ 0 ].shape [ 0 ] // output_dim stine_l = np.reshape (data [ 0 ],(output_dim,trace_dim,input_dim)) if data [ 1 ] is None:stine_r = stine_l else:stine_r = np.reshape (data [ 1 ],(output_dim,trace_dim,input_dim)) return np.reshape (np.einsum ('iAj,kAl->jilk',stine_l,stine_r.conj ()),2 * [ input_dim * output_dim ])

originalComment: Transform Kraus representation to Stinespring representation.
codeComment: This function converts a list of Kraus operators into a pair of Stinespring matrices. It iterates over each Kraus operator, constructs a Stinespring matrix by applying the operator to a basis vector, and stores the result in a list. Finally, it returns the list as a tuple.
codeFunctions: def _kraus_to_stinespring (data,input_dim,output_dim):stine_pair = [ None,None ] for i,kraus in enumerate (data):if kraus is not None:num_kraus = len (kraus) stine = np.zeros ((output_dim * num_kraus,input_dim),dtype = complex) for j,mat in enumerate (kraus):vec = np.zeros (num_kraus) vec [ j ] = 1 stine += np.kron (mat,vec [:,None ]) stine_pair [ i ] = stine return tuple (stine_pair)

originalComment: Transform Kraus representation to SuperOp representation.
codeComment: This function converts a list of Kraus operators into a superoperator. If there is only one Kraus operator, it squares it. If there are two Kraus operators, it performs a tensor product of the conjugate of the first operator with the second operator and adds it to the superoperator.
codeFunctions: def _kraus_to_superop (data,input_dim,output_dim):kraus_l,kraus_r = data superop = 0 if kraus_r is None:for i in kraus_l:superop += np.kron (np.conj (i),i) else:for i,j in zip (kraus_l,kraus_r):superop += np.kron (np.conj (j),i) return superop

originalComment: Reravel two bipartite matrices.
codeComment: This function takes two matrices, `mat1` and `mat2`, along with their respective shapes, `shape1` and `shape2`. It reshuffles the indices of the matrices and performs a tensor product to combine them. The reshaped matrices are then transposed and reshaped again to match the final shape, which is the product of the reshuffled dimensions. The result is a new matrix that is the tensor product of the input matrices.
codeFunctions: def _reravel (mat1,mat2,shape1,shape2):# Reshuffle indicies left_dims = shape1 [:2 ] + shape2 [:2 ] right_dims = shape1 [ 2:] + shape2 [ 2:] tensor_shape = left_dims + right_dims final_shape = (np.product (left_dims),np.product (right_dims)) # Tensor product matrices data = np.kron (mat1,mat2) data = np.reshape (np.transpose (np.reshape (data,tensor_shape),(0,2,1,3,4,6,5,7)),final_shape) return data

originalComment: Change of basis of bipartite matrix represenation.
codeComment: This function transforms input data from the Pauli basis to the computational basis using a change of basis matrix. It involves repeated Kronecker products and reshaping to handle multiple qubits, and then normalizes the result.
codeFunctions: def _transform_from_pauli (data,num_qubits):# Change basis: sum_{i=0}^3 =|\sigma_i>><i| basis_mat = np.array ([ [ 1,0,0,1 ],[ 0,1,1j,0 ],[ 0,1,- 1j,0 ],[ 1,0j,0,- 1 ] ],dtype = complex) # Note that we manually renormalized after change of basis # to avoid rounding errors from square-roots of 2. cob = basis_mat for _ in range (num_qubits - 1):dim = int (np.sqrt (len (cob))) cob = np.reshape (np.transpose (np.reshape (np.kron (basis_mat,cob),(2,2,dim,dim,4,dim * dim)),(0,2,1,3,4,5)),(4 * dim * dim,4 * dim * dim)) return np.dot (np.dot (cob,data),cob.conj ().T) / 2 ** num_qubits

originalComment: Return true if dims correspond to an n - qubit channel.
codeComment: This function checks if the input and output dimensions of a quantum channel are equal and if the input dimension is a power of 2, which are necessary conditions for the channel to be an n-qubit channel. If the input dimensions are not equal or if the input dimension is not a power of 2, it raises a QiskitError with an appropriate message.
codeFunctions: def _check_nqubit_dim (input_dim,output_dim):if input_dim != output_dim:raise QiskitError ('Not an n-qubit channel: input_dim' + ' ({}) != output_dim ({})'.format (input_dim,output_dim)) num_qubits = int (np.log2 (input_dim)) if 2 ** num_qubits != input_dim:raise QiskitError ('Not an n-qubit channel: input_dim != 2 ** n')

originalComment: Set x y and z labels according to one of conventions.
codeComment: This function sets the label convention for a quantum system based on the input string `convention`. It defines different label conventions for different types of quantum states and measurements, such as the original convention, XYZ convention, spin convention, 01 convention, polarization Jones convention, polarization Jones letters convention, and polarization Stokes convention. The function uses LaTeX formatting to create the labels for the x, y, and z axes.
codeFunctions: def set_label_convention (self,convention):ketex = "$\\left.|%s\\right\\rangle$" # \left.| is on purpose, so that every ket has the same size if convention == "original":self.xlabel = [ '$x$','' ] self.ylabel = [ '$y$','' ] self.zlabel = [ '$\\left|0\\right>$','$\\left|1\\right>$' ] elif convention == "xyz":self.xlabel = [ '$x$','' ] self.ylabel = [ '$y$','' ] self.zlabel = [ '$z$','' ] elif convention == "sx sy sz":self.xlabel = [ '$s_x$','' ] self.ylabel = [ '$s_y$','' ] self.zlabel = [ '$s_z$','' ] elif convention == "01":self.xlabel = [ '','' ] self.ylabel = [ '','' ] self.zlabel = [ '$\\left|0\\right>$','$\\left|1\\right>$' ] elif convention == "polarization jones":self.xlabel = [ ketex % "\\nearrow\\hspace{-1.46}\\swarrow",ketex % "\\nwarrow\\hspace{-1.46}\\searrow" ] self.ylabel = [ ketex % "\\circlearrowleft",ketex % "\\circlearrowright" ] self.zlabel = [ ketex % "\\leftrightarrow",ketex % "\\updownarrow" ] elif convention == "polarization jones letters":self.xlabel = [ ketex % "D",ketex % "A" ] self.ylabel = [ ketex % "L",ketex % "R" ] self.zlabel = [ ketex % "H",ketex % "V" ] elif convention == "polarization stokes":self.ylabel = [ "$\\nearrow\\hspace{-1.46}\\swarrow$","$\\nwarrow\\hspace{-1.46}\\searrow$" ] self.zlabel = [ "$\\circlearrowleft$","$\\circlearrowright$" ] self.xlabel = [ "$\\leftrightarrow$","$\\updownarrow$" ] else:raise Exception ("No such convention.")

It calculates the zero offset by creating a Gaussian with the given parameters and subtracts it from the input samples. If the rescale amplitude flag is set, it scales the amplitude of the Gaussian samples. If the return scale factor flag is set, it returns both the scaled Gaussian samples and the scale factor. codeFunctions: def _fix_gaussian_width (gaussian_samples,amp:float,center:float,sigma:float,zeroed_width:Union [ None,float ] = None,rescale_amp:bool = False,ret_scale_factor:bool = False) -> np.ndarray:if zeroed_width is None:zeroed_width = 2 * (center + 1) zero_offset = gaussian (np.array ([ - zeroed_width / 2 ]),amp,center,sigma) gaussian_samples -= zero_offset amp_scale_factor = 1. if rescale_amp:amp_scale_factor = amp / (amp - zero_offset) gaussian_samples *= amp_scale_factor if ret_scale_factor:return gaussian_samples,amp_scale_factor return gaussian_samples

originalComment: r Continuous unnormalized gaussian pulse.
codeComment: This function generates a Gaussian function based on the given parameters. It takes in an array of times, an amplitude, a center, a standard deviation, an optional zeroed width, a boolean flag to rescale the amplitude, and a boolean flag to return the x values. The function first converts the times array to a complex array, then calculates the Gaussian function using the provided parameters. If a zeroed width is specified, it adjusts the Gaussian function accordingly. Finally, it returns the Gaussian function and the x values if the ret_x flag is set to True.
codeFunctions: def gaussian (times:np.ndarray,amp:complex,center:float,sigma:float,zeroed_width:Union [ None,float ] = None,rescale_amp:bool = False,ret_x:bool = False) -> Union [ np.ndarray,Tuple [ np.ndarray,np.ndarray ] ]:times = np.asarray (times,dtype = np.complex_) x = (times - center) / sigma gauss = amp * np.exp (- x ** 2 / 2).astype (np.complex_) if zeroed_width is not None:gauss = _fix_gaussian_width (gauss,amp = amp,center = center,sigma = sigma,zeroed_width = zeroed_width,rescale_amp = rescale_amp) if ret_x:return gauss,x return gauss

codeComment: This function calculates the derivative of a Gaussian function with respect to time. It takes in the time array `times`, amplitude `amp`, center `center`, and standard deviation `sigma` as inputs. The function returns the derivative of the Gaussian function at each time point. If `ret_gaussian` is set to `True`, it also returns the Gaussian function itself.
codeFunctions: def gaussian_deriv (times:np.ndarray,amp:complex,center:float,sigma:float,ret_gaussian:bool = False) -> np.ndarray:gauss,x = gaussian (times,amp = amp,center = center,sigma = sigma,ret_x = True) gauss_deriv = - x / sigma * gauss if ret_gaussian:return gauss_deriv,gauss return gauss_deriv

originalComment: r Continuous gaussian square pulse.
codeComment: This function generates a piecewise function that consists of a Gaussian centered at `square_start` and `square_stop`, and a constant function with amplitude `amp`. The Gaussian functions are scaled by `rescale_amp` if set to `True`. The function is defined over the range from `square_start` to `square_stop`.
codeFunctions: def gaussian_square (times:np.ndarray,amp:complex,center:float,width:float,sigma:float,zeroed_width:Union [ None,float ] = None) -> np.ndarray:square_start = center - width / 2 square_stop = center + width / 2 if zeroed_width:zeroed_width = min (width,zeroed_width) gauss_zeroed_width = zeroed_width - width else:gauss_zeroed_width = None funclist = [ functools.partial (gaussian,amp = amp,center = square_start,sigma = sigma,zeroed_width = gauss_zeroed_width,rescale_amp = True),functools.partial (gaussian,amp = amp,center = square_stop,sigma = sigma,zeroed_width = gauss_zeroed_width,rescale_amp = True),functools.partial (constant,amp = amp) ] condlist = [ times <= square_start,times >= square_stop ] return np.piecewise (times.astype (np.complex_),condlist,funclist)

originalComment: The default pass manager that maps to the coupling map.
codeComment: This function creates a pass manager for transpiling quantum circuits. It initializes the pass manager with various passes to optimize the circuit, including unrolling, trivial layout, check map, dense layout, full ancilla allocation, enlarge with ancilla, unroll 3-qubit or more, legacy swap, expand swaps, decompose swap gate, change CX directions, unroll to basis, and simplify single qubit gates and CXs. The pass manager uses a property set to keep track of the current layout and other properties, and it applies the passes in a specific order based on the current property set.
codeFunctions: def default_pass_manager (basis_gates,coupling_map,initial_layout,seed_transpiler):pass_manager = PassManager () pass_manager.property_set [ 'layout' ] = initial_layout pass_manager.append (Unroller (basis_gates)) # Use the trivial layout if no layout is found pass_manager.append (TrivialLayout (coupling_map),condition = lambda property_set:not property_set [ 'layout' ]) # if the circuit and layout already satisfy the coupling_constraints, use that layout # otherwise layout on the most densely connected physical qubit subset pass_manager.append (CheckMap (coupling_map)) pass_manager.append (DenseLayout (coupling_map),condition = lambda property_set:not property_set [ 'is_swap_mapped' ]) # Extend the the dag/layout with ancillas using the full coupling map pass_manager.append (FullAncillaAllocation (coupling_map)) pass_manager.append (EnlargeWithAncilla ()) # Circuit must only contain 1- or 2-qubit interactions for swapper to work pass_manager.append (Unroll3qOrMore ()) # Swap mapper pass_manager.append (LegacySwap (coupling_map,trials = 20,seed = seed_transpiler)) # Expand swaps pass_manager.append (Decompose (SwapGate)) # Change CX directions pass_manager.append (CXDirection (coupling_map)) # Unroll to the basis pass_manager.append (Unroller ([ 'u1','u2','u3','id','cx' ])) # Simplify single qubit gates and CXs simplification_passes = [ Optimize1qGates (),CXCancellation (),RemoveResetInZeroState () ] pass_manager.append (simplification_passes + [ Depth (),FixedPoint ('depth') ],do_while = lambda property_set:not property_set [ 'depth_fixed_point' ]) return pass_manager

codeFunctions: def default_pass_manager_simulator (basis_gates):pass_manager = PassManager () pass_manager.append (Unroller (basis_gates)) pass_manager.append ([ RemoveResetInZeroState (),Depth (),FixedPoint ('depth') ],do_while = lambda property_set:not property_set [ 'depth_fixed_point' ]) return pass_manager

It then checks for duplicate qubits and classical bits, and raises an error if the instruction does not match the number of qubits and classical bits specified in the circuit. The function adds the instruction to the circuit's data and tracks any parameters used in the instruction.
codeFunctions: def append (self,instruction,qargs = None,cargs = None):qargs = qargs or [ ] cargs = cargs or [ ] # Convert input to instruction if not isinstance (instruction,Instruction) and hasattr (instruction,'to_instruction'):instruction = instruction.to_instruction () if not isinstance (instruction,Instruction):raise QiskitError ('object is not an Instruction.') # do some compatibility checks self._check_dups (qargs) self._check_qargs (qargs) self._check_cargs (cargs) if instruction.num_qubits != len (qargs) or instruction.num_clbits != len (cargs):raise QiskitError ("instruction %s with %d qubits and %d clbits " "cannot be appended onto %d qubits and %d clbits." % (instruction.name,instruction.num_qubits,instruction.num_clbits,len (qargs),len (cargs))) # add the instruction onto the given wires instruction_context = instruction,qargs,cargs self.data.append (instruction_context) # track variable parameters in instruction for param_index,param in enumerate (instruction.params):if isinstance (param,Parameter):current_symbols = self.parameters if param in current_symbols:self._parameter_table [ param ].append ((instruction,param_index)) else:self._parameter_table [ param ] = [ (instruction,param_index) ] return instruction

" If Integers, up to 2 arguments. QuantumCircuit was called" " with %s." % (regs,)) for register in regs:if register in self.qregs or register in self.cregs:raise QiskitError ("register name \"%s\" already exists" % register.name) if isinstance (register,QuantumRegister):self.qregs.append (register) elif isinstance (register,ClassicalRegister):self.cregs.append (register) else:raise QiskitError ("expected a register")

def qasm (self):string_temp = self.header + "
" string_temp += self.extension_lib + "

originalComment: How many non - entangled subcircuits can the circuit be factored to.
codeComment: This function calculates the number of connected components in a quantum circuit. It iterates over the gates in the circuit, updating the subgraphs based on the connections between qubits and classical bits. If a gate connects multiple subgraphs, it merges them into a single subgraph. The function returns the number of remaining subgraphs.
codeFunctions: def num_connected_components (self,unitary_only = False):# Convert registers to ints (as done in depth). reg_offset = 0 reg_map = { } if unitary_only:regs = self.qregs else:regs = self.qregs + self.cregs for reg in regs:reg_map [ reg.name ] = reg_offset reg_offset += reg.size # Start with each qubit or cbit being its own subgraph. sub_graphs = [ [ bit ] for bit in range (reg_offset) ] num_sub_graphs = len (sub_graphs) # Here we are traversing the gates and looking to see # which of the sub_graphs the gate joins together. for instr,qargs,cargs in self.data:if unitary_only:args = qargs num_qargs = len (args) else:args = qargs + cargs num_qargs = len (args) + (1 if instr.control else 0) if num_qargs >= 2 and instr.name not in [ 'barrier','snapshot' ]:graphs_touched = [ ] num_touched = 0 # Controls necessarily join all the cbits in the # register that they use. if instr.control and not unitary_only:creg = instr.control [ 0 ] creg_int = reg_map [ creg.name ] for coff in range (creg.size):temp_int = creg_int + coff for k in range (num_sub_graphs):if temp_int in sub_graphs [ k ]:graphs_touched.append (k) num_touched += 1 break for item in args:reg_int = reg_map [ item [ 0 ].name ] + item [ 1 ] for k in range (num_sub_graphs):if reg_int in sub_graphs [ k ]:if k not in graphs_touched:graphs_touched.append (k) num_touched += 1 break # If the gate touches more than one subgraph # join those graphs together and return # reduced number of subgraphs if num_touched > 1:connections = [ ] for idx in graphs_touched:connections.extend (sub_graphs [ idx ]) _sub_graphs = [ ] for idx in range (num_sub_graphs):if idx not in graphs_touched:_sub_graphs.append (sub_graphs [ idx ]) _sub_graphs.append (connections) sub_graphs = _sub_graphs num_sub_graphs -= (num_touched - 1) # Cannot go lower than one so break if num_sub_graphs == 1:break return num_sub_graphs

codeFunctions: def pulse_drawer (samples,duration,dt = None,interp_method = 'None',filename = None,interactive = False,dpi = 150,nop = 1000,size = (6,5)):try:from matplotlib import pyplot as plt except ImportError:raise ImportError ('pulse_drawer need matplotlib. ' 'Run "pip install matplotlib" before.') if dt:_dt = dt else:_dt = 1 re_y = np.real (samples) im_y = np.imag (samples) image = plt.figure (figsize = size) ax0 = image.add_subplot (111) if interp_method == 'CubicSpline':# spline interpolation, use mid-point of dt time = np.arange (0,duration + 1) * _dt + 0.5 * _dt cs_ry = CubicSpline (time [:- 1 ],re_y) cs_iy = CubicSpline (time [:- 1 ],im_y) _time = np.linspace (0,duration * _dt,nop) _re_y = cs_ry (_time) _im_y = cs_iy (_time) elif interp_method == 'None':# pseudo-DAC output time = np.arange (0,duration + 1) * _dt _time = np.r_ [ time [ 0 ],np.repeat (time [ 1:- 1 ],2),time [ - 1 ] ] _re_y = np.repeat (re_y,2) _im_y = np.repeat (im_y,2) else:raise QiskitError ('Invalid interpolation method "%s"' % interp_method) # plot ax0.fill_between (x = _time,y1 = _re_y,y2 = np.zeros_like (_time),facecolor = 'red',alpha = 0.3,edgecolor = 'red',linewidth = 1.5,label = 'real part') ax0.fill_between (x = _time,y1 = _im_y,y2 = np.zeros_like (_time),facecolor = 'blue',alpha = 0.3,edgecolor = 'blue',linewidth = 1.5,label = 'imaginary part') ax0.set_xlim (0,duration * _dt) ax0.grid (b = True,linestyle = '-') ax0.legend (bbox_to_anchor = (0.5,1.00),loc = 'lower center',ncol = 2,frameon = False,fontsize = 14) if filename:image.savefig (filename,dpi = dpi,bbox_inches = 'tight') plt.close (image) if image and interactive:plt.show (image) return image

originalComment: Search for SWAPs which allow for application of largest number of gates.
codeComment:
This function `_search_forward_n_swaps` is a recursive algorithm designed to find the best sequence of swaps to map free gates onto a layout while minimizing the distance between gates. Here's a summary of the function:

1. **Initialization**:
   - The function takes parameters: `layout`, `gates`, `coupling_map`, `depth`, and `width`.
   - It maps free gates onto the layout using `_map_free_gates` and initializes the base step with the current layout, number of swaps added, mapped gates, and remaining gates.

2. **Base Case**:
   - If there are no remaining gates or the depth is zero, it returns the base step.

3. **Possible Swaps**:
   - It retrieves possible swaps from the `coupling_map`.

4. **Scoring Swaps**:
   - The `_score_swap` function calculates the relative score for a given swap by creating a trial layout, applying the swap, and calculating the layout distance.

5. **Ranking Swaps**:
   - The possible swaps are ranked based on their scores.

6. **Selecting the Best Swap**:
   - It iterates over the top `width` ranked swaps, applies each swap to a trial layout, and recursively calls `_search_forward_n_swaps` to find the best next step.
   - It keeps track of the best swap and the corresponding step based on the score.

7. **Updating the Best Swap**:
   - If a better swap is found, it updates the best swap and the corresponding step.

8. **Returning the Result**:
   - It returns the best step, including the updated layout, number of swaps added, remaining gates, and mapped gates.

This function is used to find the optimal sequence of swaps to map gates onto a layout, ensuring that the gates are placed as close as possible to their target positions.
codeFunctions: def _search_forward_n_swaps (layout,gates,coupling_map,depth = SEARCH_DEPTH,width = SEARCH_WIDTH):gates_mapped,gates_remaining = _map_free_gates (layout,gates,coupling_map) base_step = { 'layout':layout,'swaps_added':0,'gates_mapped':gates_mapped,'gates_remaining':gates_remaining } if not gates_remaining or depth == 0:return base_step possible_swaps = coupling_map.get_edges () def _score_swap (swap):"""Calculate the relative score for a given SWAP.""" trial_layout = layout.copy () trial_layout.swap (* swap) return _calc_layout_distance (gates,coupling_map,trial_layout) ranked_swaps = sorted (possible_swaps,key = _score_swap) best_swap,best_step = None,None for swap in ranked_swaps [:width ]:trial_layout = layout.copy () trial_layout.swap (* swap) next_step = _search_forward_n_swaps (trial_layout,gates_remaining,coupling_map,depth - 1,width) # ranked_swaps already sorted by distance, so distance is the tie-breaker. if best_swap is None or _score_step (next_step) > _score_step (best_step):best_swap,best_step = swap,next_step best_swap_gate = _swap_ops_from_edge (best_swap,layout) return { 'layout':best_step [ 'layout' ],'swaps_added':1 + best_step [ 'swaps_added' ],'gates_remaining':best_step [ 'gates_remaining' ],'gates_mapped':gates_mapped + best_swap_gate + best_step [ 'gates_mapped' ],}

originalComment: Map all gates that can be executed with the current layout.
codeComment: This function maps free gates in a quantum circuit to a specific layout while considering blocked qubits and coupling map distances. It iterates through each gate, checks if it has a partition, and then determines if the gate's qubits are blocked or if they can be mapped directly. If the qubits are blocked, they are added to the `blocked_qubits` set and the gate is added to the `remaining_gates` list. If the qubits are not blocked, the gate is transformed for the layout and added to the `mapped_gates` list. The function returns the lists of mapped and remaining gates.
codeFunctions: def _map_free_gates (layout,gates,coupling_map):blocked_qubits = set () mapped_gates = [ ] remaining_gates = [ ] for gate in gates:# Gates without a partition (barrier, snapshot, save, load, noise) may # still have associated qubits. Look for them in the qargs. if not gate [ 'partition' ]:qubits = [ n for n in gate [ 'graph' ].nodes () if n.type == 'op' ] [ 0 ].qargs if not qubits:continue if blocked_qubits.intersection (qubits):blocked_qubits.update (qubits) remaining_gates.append (gate) else:mapped_gate = _transform_gate_for_layout (gate,layout) mapped_gates.append (mapped_gate) continue qubits = gate [ 'partition' ] [ 0 ] if blocked_qubits.intersection (qubits):blocked_qubits.update (qubits) remaining_gates.append (gate) elif len (qubits) == 1:mapped_gate = _transform_gate_for_layout (gate,layout) mapped_gates.append (mapped_gate) elif coupling_map.distance (* [ layout [ q ] for q in qubits ]) == 1:mapped_gate = _transform_gate_for_layout (gate,layout) mapped_gates.append (mapped_gate) else:blocked_qubits.update (qubits) remaining_gates.append (gate) return mapped_gates,remaining_gates

originalComment: Return the sum of the distances of two - qubit pairs in each CNOT in gates according to the layout and the coupling.
codeComment: This function calculates the total distance between gates in a quantum circuit based on their layout and coupling map. It sums up the distances between pairs of qubits in each gate's partition, considering only the first two qubits in each partition. The function takes a list of gates, a coupling map, a layout, and an optional maximum number of gates to consider. If no maximum is provided, it defaults to 50 plus 10 times the number of physical qubits in the coupling map.
codeFunctions: def _calc_layout_distance (gates,coupling_map,layout,max_gates = None):if max_gates is None:max_gates = 50 + 10 * len (coupling_map.physical_qubits) return sum (coupling_map.distance (* [ layout [ q ] for q in gate [ 'partition' ] [ 0 ] ]) for gate in gates [:max_gates ] if gate [ 'partition' ] and len (gate [ 'partition' ] [ 0 ]) == 2)

codeFunctions: def _score_step (step):# Each added swap will add 3 ops to gates_mapped, so subtract 3. return len ([ g for g in step [ 'gates_mapped' ] if len (g.qargs) == 2 ]) - 3 * step [ 'swaps_added' ]

originalComment: Run one pass of the lookahead mapper on the provided DAG.
codeComment: This function takes a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) and a coupling map as input, and returns a mapped DAG using the forward n-swap algorithm. It first checks if the initial layout is provided, and if not, generates a trivial layout. It then checks if the layout matches the number of qubits in the DAG and if the coupling map has the same number of physical qubits as the layout. The function then iteratively applies the forward n-swap algorithm to map the gates in the DAG to the coupling map, and returns the mapped DAG.
codeFunctions: def run (self,dag):coupling_map = self._coupling_map ordered_virtual_gates = list (dag.serial_layers ()) if self.initial_layout is None:if self.property_set [ "layout" ]:self.initial_layout = self.property_set [ "layout" ] else:self.initial_layout = Layout.generate_trivial_layout (* dag.qregs.values ()) if len (dag.qubits ()) != len (self.initial_layout):raise TranspilerError ('The layout does not match the amount of qubits in the DAG') if len (self._coupling_map.physical_qubits) != len (self.initial_layout):raise TranspilerError ("Mappers require to have the layout to be the same size as the coupling map") mapped_gates = [ ] layout = self.initial_layout.copy () gates_remaining = ordered_virtual_gates.copy () while gates_remaining:best_step = _search_forward_n_swaps (layout,gates_remaining,coupling_map) layout = best_step [ 'layout' ] gates_mapped = best_step [ 'gates_mapped' ] gates_remaining = best_step [ 'gates_remaining' ] mapped_gates.extend (gates_mapped) # Preserve input DAG's name, regs, wire_map, etc. but replace the graph. mapped_dag = _copy_circuit_metadata (dag,coupling_map) for node in mapped_gates:mapped_dag.apply_operation_back (op = node.op,qargs = node.qargs,cargs = node.cargs) return mapped_dag

originalComment: Compute the full distance matrix on pairs of nodes.
codeComment: This function computes the distance matrix for a coupling graph. It first checks if the graph is connected. If not, it raises a CouplingError. It then calculates the shortest path lengths between all pairs of nodes using the `all_pairs_shortest_path_length` function from the NetworkX library. The lengths are stored in a dictionary and converted to a numpy array. The array is then used to create a distance matrix, which is stored in the `_dist_matrix` attribute of the object.
codeFunctions: def _compute_distance_matrix (self):if not self.is_connected ():raise CouplingError ("coupling graph not connected") lengths = nx.all_pairs_shortest_path_length (self.graph.to_undirected (as_view = True)) lengths = dict (lengths) size = len (lengths) cmap = np.zeros ((size,size)) for idx in range (size):cmap [ idx,np.fromiter (lengths [ idx ].keys (),dtype = int) ] = np.fromiter (lengths [ idx ].values (),dtype = int) self._dist_matrix = cmap

If the distance matrix is not computed yet, it computes it using the `_compute_distance_matrix` method. Finally, it returns the distance between the two qubits from the computed distance matrix.

originalComment: Emits an event if there are any subscribers.
codeComment:
The `dispatch` method in the given code is designed to handle events and notify subscribers. Here's a summary of its functionality:

- **Parameters**:
  - `self`: The instance of the class.
  - `event`: The event to be dispatched.
  - `*args`: Variable positional arguments to be passed to the subscriber's callback.
  - `**kwargs`: Variable keyword arguments to be passed to the subscriber's callback.

- **Logic**:
  - The method first checks if the `event` is present in the `_subscribers` dictionary.
  - If the event is not found, it returns immediately without executing any further code.
  - If the event is found, it iterates over the list of subscribers associated with that event.
  - For each subscriber, it calls the `callback` method with the provided `*args` and `**kwargs`.

- **Purpose**:
  - The method is used to trigger events and notify all subscribers that are registered for that event.
  - It allows for flexible event handling by allowing subscribers to register for multiple events and receive notifications for each one.

This method is typically used in event-driven programming frameworks where events are triggered and subscribers are notified accordingly.
codeFunctions: def dispatch (self,event,* args,* * kwargs):# No event, no subscribers. if event not in self._subscribers:return for subscriber in self._subscribers [ event ]:subscriber.callback (* args,* * kwargs)

originalComment: Calculate a subcircuit that implements this initialization
codeComment: This method defines a quantum circuit to initialize a quantum register to a desired state by first generating a circuit to uncompute the desired state, inverting it to create the desired state from zero, and then appending a reset operation followed by the inverted circuit to the quantum register. The resulting circuit is stored in the `definition` attribute.

originalComment: Call to create a circuit with gates that take the desired vector to zero.
codeComment: This function generates a quantum circuit to disentangle qubits in a quantum register. It iterates over each qubit, calculates the necessary rotations to disentangle it, and appends the corresponding gates to the circuit. The circuit is named 'disentangler'.
codeFunctions: def gates_to_uncompute (self):q = QuantumRegister (self.num_qubits) circuit = QuantumCircuit (q,name = 'disentangler') # kick start the peeling loop, and disentangle one-by-one from LSB to MSB remaining_param = self.params for i in range (self.num_qubits):# work out which rotations must be done to disentangle the LSB # qubit (we peel away one qubit at a time) (remaining_param,thetas,phis) = Initialize._rotations_to_disentangle (remaining_param) # perform the required rotations to decouple the LSB qubit (so that # it can be "factored" out, leaving a shorter amplitude vector to peel away) rz_mult = self._multiplex (RZGate,phis) ry_mult = self._multiplex (RYGate,thetas) circuit.append (rz_mult.to_instruction (),q [ i:self.num_qubits ]) circuit.append (ry_mult.to_instruction (),q [ i:self.num_qubits ]) return circuit

originalComment: Static internal method to work out rotation to create the passed in qubit from the zero vector.
codeComment: This function calculates the Bloch angles for a pair of complex numbers. It first ensures that the inputs are complex numbers, then computes the magnitude of the first complex number and the magnitude of the second complex number. If the sum of the magnitudes squared is less than a small threshold (_EPS), it returns zero for all angles. Otherwise, it calculates the theta and phi angles using the arccosine and angle functions from the numpy library, respectively. Finally, it returns the Bloch vector and the calculated angles.
codeFunctions: def _bloch_angles (pair_of_complex):[ a_complex,b_complex ] = pair_of_complex # Force a and b to be complex, as otherwise numpy.angle might fail. a_complex = complex (a_complex) b_complex = complex (b_complex) mag_a = np.absolute (a_complex) final_r = float (np.sqrt (mag_a ** 2 + np.absolute (b_complex) ** 2)) if final_r < _EPS:theta = 0 phi = 0 final_r = 0 final_t = 0 else:theta = float (2 * np.arccos (mag_a / final_r)) a_arg = np.angle (a_complex) b_arg = np.angle (b_complex) final_t = a_arg + b_arg phi = b_arg - a_arg return final_r * np.exp (1.J * final_t / 2),theta,phi

originalComment: Return a recursive implementation of a multiplexor circuit where each instruction itself has a decomposition based on smaller multiplexors.
codeComment: This function is a recursive quantum circuit generator for a multiplexing operation. It takes a target gate and a list of angles as input. The function calculates the angle weights using a Kronecker product and identity matrix, then recursively processes the angles. It constructs a quantum circuit with a quantum register of the appropriate size, applies the target gate to the least significant bit (LSB), and uses CNOT gates to implement the multiplexing. The function handles the base case when the number of qubits is 1 and recursively processes the angles for higher numbers of qubits.
codeFunctions: def _multiplex (self,target_gate,list_of_angles):list_len = len (list_of_angles) local_num_qubits = int (math.log2 (list_len)) + 1 q = QuantumRegister (local_num_qubits) circuit = QuantumCircuit (q,name = "multiplex" + local_num_qubits.__str__ ()) lsb = q [ 0 ] msb = q [ local_num_qubits - 1 ] # case of no multiplexing: base case for recursion if local_num_qubits == 1:circuit.append (target_gate (list_of_angles [ 0 ]),[ q [ 0 ] ]) return circuit # calc angle weights, assuming recursion (that is the lower-level # requested angles have been correctly implemented by recursion angle_weight = scipy.kron ([ [ 0.5,0.5 ],[ 0.5,- 0.5 ] ],np.identity (2 ** (local_num_qubits - 2))) # calc the combo angles list_of_angles = angle_weight.dot (np.array (list_of_angles)).tolist () # recursive step on half the angles fulfilling the above assumption multiplex_1 = self._multiplex (target_gate,list_of_angles [ 0:(list_len // 2) ]) circuit.append (multiplex_1.to_instruction (),q [ 0:- 1 ]) # attach CNOT as follows, thereby flipping the LSB qubit circuit.append (CnotGate (),[ msb,lsb ]) # implement extra efficiency from the paper of cancelling adjacent # CNOTs (by leaving out last CNOT and reversing (NOT inverting) the # second lower-level multiplex) multiplex_2 = self._multiplex (target_gate,list_of_angles [ (list_len // 2):]) if list_len > 1:circuit.append (multiplex_2.to_instruction ().mirror (),q [ 0:- 1 ]) else:circuit.append (multiplex_2.to_instruction (),q [ 0:- 1 ]) # attach a final CNOT circuit.append (CnotGate (),[ msb,lsb ]) return circuit

codeComment: This function updates a quantum circuit by composing layers based on a given layout and best circuit. It handles the first layer with multi-qubit gates and outputs all layers up to that point, ignoring swap gates. For subsequent layers, it outputs the current layer and any associated swap gates. The function uses a DAGCircuit to construct the updated circuit.
codeFunctions: def _layer_update (self,i,first_layer,best_layout,best_depth,best_circuit,layer_list):layout = best_layout logger.debug ("layer_update: layout = %s",pformat (layout)) logger.debug ("layer_update: self.initial_layout = %s",pformat (self.initial_layout)) dagcircuit_output = DAGCircuit () for register in layout.get_virtual_bits ().keys ():if register [ 0 ] not in dagcircuit_output.qregs.values ():dagcircuit_output.add_qreg (register [ 0 ]) # If this is the first layer with multi-qubit gates, # output all layers up to this point and ignore any # swap gates. Set the initial layout. if first_layer:logger.debug ("layer_update: first multi-qubit gate layer") # Output all layers up to this point for j in range (i + 1):# Make qubit edge map and extend by classical bits edge_map = layout.combine_into_edge_map (self.initial_layout) for bit in dagcircuit_output.clbits ():edge_map [ bit ] = bit dagcircuit_output.compose_back (layer_list [ j ] [ "graph" ],edge_map) # Otherwise, we output the current layer and the associated swap gates. else:# Output any swaps if best_depth > 0:logger.debug ("layer_update: there are swaps in this layer, " "depth %d",best_depth) dagcircuit_output.extend_back (best_circuit) else:logger.debug ("layer_update: there are no swaps in this layer") # Make qubit edge map and extend by classical bits edge_map = layout.combine_into_edge_map (self.initial_layout) for bit in dagcircuit_output.clbits ():edge_map [ bit ] = bit # Output this layer dagcircuit_output.compose_back (layer_list [ i ] [ "graph" ],edge_map) return dagcircuit_output

originalComment: Return the Pauli group with 4^n elements.
codeComment: This function generates the Pauli group for a given number of qubits. It supports two cases: 'weight' and 'tensor'. In the 'weight' case, it sorts the Pauli operators based on their weight (number of non-identity Pauli operators). In the 'tensor' case, it generates the Pauli operators in tensor order. The function raises a QiskitError if the number of qubits is greater than or equal to 5 or if an unsupported case is provided.
codeFunctions: def pauli_group (number_of_qubits,case = 'weight'):if number_of_qubits < 5:temp_set = [ ] if case == 'weight':tmp = pauli_group (number_of_qubits,case = 'tensor') # sort on the weight of the Pauli operator return sorted (tmp,key = lambda x:- np.count_nonzero (np.array (x.to_label (),'c') == b'I')) elif case == 'tensor':# the Pauli set is in tensor order II IX IY IZ XI ... for k in range (4 ** number_of_qubits):z = np.zeros (number_of_qubits,dtype = np.bool) x = np.zeros (number_of_qubits,dtype = np.bool) # looping over all the qubits for j in range (number_of_qubits):# making the Pauli for each j fill it in from the # end first element = (k // (4 ** j)) % 4 if element == 1:x [ j ] = True elif element == 2:z [ j ] = True x [ j ] = True elif element == 3:z [ j ] = True temp_set.append (Pauli (z,x)) return temp_set else:raise QiskitError ("Only support 'weight' or 'tensor' cases " "but you have {}.".format (case)) raise QiskitError ("Only support number of qubits is less than 5")

originalComment: r Take pauli string to construct pauli.
codeComment: This function takes a string `label` as input and returns a new instance of a class with two boolean arrays `z` and `x`. The arrays are initialized to zeros with the same length as the input string. The function then iterates over each character in the input string, setting the corresponding elements in the `z` and `x` arrays based on the character. If the character is 'X', 'Y', or 'Z', it sets the corresponding element in the `z` array to True. If the character is 'I', it sets the corresponding element in the `x` array to True. If the character is not 'I', 'X', 'Y', or 'Z', it raises a `QiskitError`.
codeFunctions: def from_label (cls,label):z = np.zeros (len (label),dtype = np.bool) x = np.zeros (len (label),dtype = np.bool) for i,char in enumerate (label):if char == 'X':x [ - i - 1 ] = True elif char == 'Z':z [ - i - 1 ] = True elif char == 'Y':z [ - i - 1 ] = True x [ - i - 1 ] = True elif char != 'I':raise QiskitError ("Pauli string must be only consisted of 'I', 'X', " "'Y' or 'Z' but you have {}.".format (char)) return cls (z = z,x = x)

The vectors are then converted to NumPy boolean arrays using the `_make_np_bool` function and stored as instance variables `_z` and `_x`. Finally, the method returns the initialized object.

(z: {} vs x: {})".format (len (z),len (x))) z = _make_np_bool (z) x = _make_np_bool (x) self._z = z self._x = x return self

originalComment: Simulate the outcome of measurement of a qubit.
codeComment: This function calculates the probability of measuring a qubit in the state '0' or '1' based on the state vector of a quantum system. It first computes the probabilities of measuring the qubit in each state by summing the squares of the absolute values of the state vector elements along the appropriate axis. Then, it generates a random number and compares it to the probabilities to determine the outcome. If the random number is less than the probability of measuring '0', it returns '0' and the corresponding probability; otherwise, it returns '1' and the probability of measuring '1'.
codeFunctions: def _get_measure_outcome (self,qubit):# Axis for numpy.sum to compute probabilities axis = list (range (self._number_of_qubits)) axis.remove (self._number_of_qubits - 1 - qubit) probabilities = np.sum (np.abs (self._statevector) ** 2,axis = tuple (axis)) # Compute einsum index string for 1-qubit matrix multiplication random_number = self._local_random.rand () if random_number < probabilities [ 0 ]:return '0',probabilities [ 0 ] # Else outcome was '1' return '1',probabilities [ 1 ]

originalComment: Generate memory samples from current statevector.
codeComment: This function generates random samples from the quantum state vector based on the specified measurement parameters. It first identifies the unique qubits that are measured, then computes the probabilities of measuring each qubit. It reshapes the state vector to match the number of measured qubits and generates random samples based on these probabilities. Finally, it converts the samples into bit-strings and returns the corresponding classical memory values.
codeFunctions: def _add_sample_measure (self,measure_params,num_samples):# Get unique qubits that are actually measured measured_qubits = list ({ qubit for qubit,cmembit in measure_params }) num_measured = len (measured_qubits) # Axis for numpy.sum to compute probabilities axis = list (range (self._number_of_qubits)) for qubit in reversed (measured_qubits):# Remove from largest qubit to smallest so list position is correct # with respect to position from end of the list axis.remove (self._number_of_qubits - 1 - qubit) probabilities = np.reshape (np.sum (np.abs (self._statevector) ** 2,axis = tuple (axis)),2 ** num_measured) # Generate samples on measured qubits samples = self._local_random.choice (range (2 ** num_measured),num_samples,p = probabilities) # Convert to bit-strings memory = [ ] for sample in samples:classical_memory = self._classical_memory for count,(qubit,cmembit) in enumerate (sorted (measure_params)):qubit_outcome = int ((sample & (1 << count)) >> count) membit = 1 << cmembit classical_memory = (classical_memory & (~ membit)) | (qubit_outcome << cmembit) value = bin (classical_memory) [ 2:] memory.append (hex (int (value,2))) return memory

originalComment: Apply a measure instruction to a qubit.
codeComment: This function measures a qubit and updates the classical memory and register based on the measurement outcome. If a classical register is provided, it also updates the register. The function then applies a unitary transformation to the qubit based on the measurement outcome.
codeFunctions: def _add_qasm_measure (self,qubit,cmembit,cregbit = None):# get measure outcome outcome,probability = self._get_measure_outcome (qubit) # update classical state membit = 1 << cmembit self._classical_memory = (self._classical_memory & (~ membit)) | (int (outcome) << cmembit) if cregbit is not None:regbit = 1 << cregbit self._classical_register = (self._classical_register & (~ regbit)) | (int (outcome) << cregbit) # update quantum state if outcome == '0':update_diag = [ [ 1 / np.sqrt (probability),0 ],[ 0,0 ] ] else:update_diag = [ [ 0,0 ],[ 0,1 / np.sqrt (probability) ] ] # update classical state self._add_unitary_single (update_diag,qubit)

If the measurement outcome is '0', it applies a Hadamard gate to the qubit, resulting in a superposition of |0⟩ and |1⟩. If the measurement outcome is '1', it applies a Pauli-X gate to the qubit, resulting in the state |1⟩.

originalComment: Determine if measure sampling is allowed for an experiment
codeComment: This function checks if measure sampling should be enabled for a given experiment. It first checks if the number of shots is 1, in which case measure sampling is disabled. Then, it checks for a configuration flag that allows measure sampling. If the flag is not found, it performs a simple test to determine if the circuit contains only measure instructions. If the circuit contains reset instructions or non-measure instructions after the first measure, measure sampling is disabled. If the circuit contains only measure instructions, measure sampling is enabled.
codeFunctions: def _validate_measure_sampling (self,experiment):# If shots=1 we should disable measure sampling. # This is also required for statevector simulator to return the # correct final statevector without silently dropping final measurements. if self._shots <= 1:self._sample_measure = False return # Check for config flag if hasattr (experiment.config,'allows_measure_sampling'):self._sample_measure = experiment.config.allows_measure_sampling # If flag isn't found do a simple test to see if a circuit contains # no reset instructions, and no gates instructions after # the first measure. else:measure_flag = False for instruction in experiment.instructions:# If circuit contains reset operations we cannot sample if instruction.name == "reset":self._sample_measure = False return # If circuit contains a measure option then we can # sample only if all following operations are measures if measure_flag:# If we find a non-measure instruction # we cannot do measure sampling if instruction.name not in [ "measure","barrier","id","u0" ]:self._sample_measure = False return elif instruction.name == "measure":measure_flag = True # If we made it to the end of the circuit without returning # measure sampling is allowed self._sample_measure = True
